scope: Domain initialization, resume and batch part authorization only. HTTP endpoints/DTO mapping, upload completion and reconciliation workers remain in their planned SIs.

implementation.ownership: JWT sub is passed as userId and resolved via ChannelsService.findByUserId; video queries always use the resolved channel id. Creation without channel is CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND; private absence or other owner is VIDEO_NOT_FOUND.
implementation.initialization: Input validated against title/filename/MIME and integer 1..10000000000 byte contract. Draft UUID/slug/source key are committed before acquiring initializing claim and before any S3 session/permission. A separate 120s initialization lease is used; no S3 request runs inside a database transaction.
implementation.session_persistence: New rememberUploadSession conditionally persists upload id/deadline while retaining initializing claim. Existing attachUploadSession conditionally releases it for use. Both use owner/token/live-lease guards and check affected rows. Returned initialization is read back from persisted state.
implementation.compensation: After a known create, failure re-reads ownership/state. An already committed attachment is recovered without abort. For a still-owned initializing claim with at least 60s remaining, abort is attempted before failUpload persists UPLOAD_INITIALIZATION_FAILED. Lost/expired claims are not overwritten or aborted. Failed abort/DB compensation preserves pending state for reconciliation. Recovered committed attachment also revalidates state and expiry before returning success.
implementation.uncertain_create: If CreateMultipartUpload succeeds remotely but its response is lost, the draft/source key and initializing claim remain recognizable even without upload id. Later orphan/session reconciliation must resolve it; no false success or destructive guess.
implementation.resume: Authoritative ListParts maps server sizes to sizeBytes and preserves id/slug. Owner, draft state, operation and expiry checked before storage access; persisted state/session re-read before returning.
implementation.permissions: 1..50 distinct integer part numbers within persisted part count. Expected size derives from declared bytes: 64MiB except exact final remainder. Session existence checked through ListParts; signer receives server-owned key/id and stored expiry. State/session checked again before returning URLs.
implementation.expiry: Expired draft checks HeadObject first. Missing object is UPLOAD_EXPIRED/410; completed object yields UPLOAD_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS/409 for later completion reconciliation. Neither path deletes session/object or mutates the draft.
implementation.errors: DomainException subclasses follow Error Catalog. Intended StorageError becomes sanitized STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE; unexpected SQL/programming failures propagate to existing 500 handling. Results contain explicit domain projections/dates, not entity objects, keys, upload ids or HTTP DTOs.
implementation.wiring: VideosModule imports ChannelsModule, VideosPersistenceModule, StorageModule and videos config, exports VideoUploadsService and is imported by AppModule. No controller or queue/worker activated.

acceptance_proofs: Real SQL read inside the S3 create boundary observes committed draft UUID/slug, owner channel and initializing claim before actual CreateMultipartUpload.
Real signed PUT uploads exact last-part bytes; repeated resume returns authoritative size/ETag, same id/slug and only one persisted video/S3 session.
Other actual channel gets VIDEO_NOT_FOUND for resume/signing without storage lookup; missing-channel creation returns CHANNEL_NOT_FOUND.
Expired session gets no new signatures and remains intact; completed source with expired DB draft is preserved and returned as pending reconciliation rather than expired/lost.
Actual SQL failures in rememberUploadSession and attachUploadSession both trigger real multipart abort and guarded initialization failure persistence.
Simulated abort outage retains actual persisted upload id and initializing claim; remote create followed by lost response leaves actual orphan discoverable by stored source key.
Attachment that commits and then loses its response is recovered; resulting session can receive a real signed PUT and resume normally.
Real claim token replacement/expiry during create makes remember CAS fail; stale initializer cannot abort or overwrite it.

Unit tests cover exact numeric 10GB boundary without video allocation, invalid controls/batches, exact full/final part sizes, state/ownership/operation guards, post-ListParts state change and typed versus unexpected failures.
Additional final-review regression: committed attachment with lost response and expired session yields UPLOAD_EXPIRED, never initialization success or a destructive abort.

limitations: Completion/outbox transition, abort/status service and HTTP controllers belong to subsequent SIs.
Preserved initializing/orphan states require the later planned reconciler; this SI does not run background recovery.
Numeric 10GB boundary coverage is not the later full valid-video 10GB transfer/processing/RSS proof.
Development HTTP server and worker not started; no commit or push performed.
